title: fix(telegram): refresh typing after delivered messages
body:
## What Problem This Solves

An immediate Telegram follow-up can miss its first typing cue after the preceding reply clears Telegram's client-side action. The account coalescer still holds its previous four-second gate; a late pending action can also restore that stale gate.

Related: #116695 and its merged lifecycle fix #116721. This repairs the remaining account-coalescer gap, not queued-turn ownership (#162684) or flood-wait logging.

## Change and User Impact

After an actual successful send/copy/forward message result, invalidate only the delivered chat/topic's action scope, using the returned topic when available. Scope-owned action maps prevent a pre-delivery pending completion from restoring the invalidated gate. An immediate new turn gets a fresh liveness cue; same-turn keepalive coalescing and other scopes retain their gates.

The contributor's production patch is unchanged. No SDK, configuration, routing, duration, flood-wait, transient-error or 401/backoff policy change. Contributor clawSean's original commit is preserved; the added commit strengthens other-chat isolation in the existing regression without adding lines.

Production delta: **+57/-9 = +48**, 66 changed lines. Tests: **+22/-22 = 0**; no allocation record or shared scalar change.

## Evidence

Exact head: `3bf27d47562cfa0e8f49b647a425b2251f983a4a`; main baseline: `65181e7147094c8b7a7217c6ca705192f3ca51d3`.

[Real Telegram Test Server userbot proof, transport correlation, controls and teardown](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191709#issuecomment-6597902240).

Built Gateway in official node:24.22.1 Docker, deterministic localhost provider, actual Test Server Bot API and TDLib userbot with Convex-leased credentials. After a warmup, the recorder sends a fast FIRST turn, observes its exact native final, and immediately sends FOLLOWUP through the maintained reply barrier. The slow follow-up exposes its typing lifecycle. Streaming is off so a progress-card delivery cannot hide the tested boundary.

| Ref | Reply → follow-up gap | First native follow-up typing | Successful typing request in first 2s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Main, run 1 | 200ms | 5155ms | 0 |
| Main, run 2 | 216ms | 5004ms | 0 |
| Exact head, run 1 | 243ms | 632ms | 1 |
| Exact head, run 2 | 177ms | 835ms | 1 |

Main eventually types, but misses the immediate cue. Both candidate runs deliver fresh native typing within 0.9s. Every follow-up is within 2.3s of the FIRST send, inside the unchanged four-second gate.

Native same-turn controls on both refs get prompt typing and three successful keepalive requests at the unchanged approximately four-second cadence. Other-chat/topic isolation and late pending completion are covered through the real coalescer + grammY transport: root delivery resets only its scope, the old completion cannot restore it, and another topic and another chat remain coalesced. Existing pending, message-budget, flood-wait and 401 controls remain.

Focused suites: **32/32 pass** on head (18.94s wall, 7.06s Vitest). Main's account transport regression: **22 pass / 1 fail** (18.67s wall, 6.53s Vitest), expecting two typing requests after delivery but receiving one. Focused formatting/lint and both builds pass; broad checks belong to PR CI.

All four accepted Gateways shut down cleanly and all five leases, including an excluded incomplete drive, released. Private payload and restored credential scratch checked absent. The incomplete repeat exhausted a 90s recorder deadline during a slow cold warmup; its capture is retained and excluded. The second pair uses a longer deadline/later control offset with the immediate-reply behavior unchanged.

The contributor's earlier broker-access gap is superseded by the real Test Server proof. A trusted host helper owns the lease; only its private payload enters Docker. A proof-only runner loader handles lease ownership and profiles, and its NODE_OPTIONS is stripped from the Gateway child. No product runtime preload, source injection, paid provider or personal Gateway.

## Boundaries and Merge Risk

This is native action-update evidence, not a Telegram Web/pixel screenshot claim. Other-chat and late-action controls are deterministic transport tests, not separately staged native chats/races. No claim to fix queued-turn typing ownership.

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the prior ephemeral coalescer behavior; no stored-state or config migration. Blast radius is Telegram's first chat action after successful message delivery. An incorrect invalidation could suppress that cue or cause extra first actions; scope, same-turn, pending-completion and unchanged-cooldown controls constrain that risk.
